usageNotes: Triggers an LDAP/AD directory sync for the specified realm, writing users and/or groups into Proxmox's user.cfg; the call returns a task UPID immediately and the sync runs asynchronously (poll with the task API to confirm completion). The realm must already be configured as an LDAP/AD domain and the caller needs both 'Realm.AllocateUser' on '/access/realm/<realm>' and 'User.Modify' on '/access/groups/'. Prefer 'remove-vanished' over the deprecated 'full'/'purge' params; synced groups are always suffixed with '-<realm>', so pre-existing groups with that naming pattern will be overwritten.

examples.summary: Sync both users and groups from the 'corp' LDAP realm, enabling new accounts and removing vanished entries and their ACLs

tips: Use 'dry-run': true first to preview what would be written without touching user.cfg — useful before the first production sync.
The returned UPID can be passed to GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to monitor completion.
Synced group names are always '<ldap-groupname>-<realm>'; ensure no manually created groups share that pattern or they will be overwritten.
'remove-vanished': 'none' (the default) is the safest option — it adds/updates but never deletes, making it idempotent for most scheduled sync jobs.
If 'enable-new' is false, newly discovered LDAP users are created in a disabled state and must be manually enabled before they can log in.
